features.title: Generalize the teaching engine so Level 4 rides shared logic, not a one-off
features.behavior: Extract the narration/highlight logic that currently only understands the single canned Linear Search instruction sequence into something that walks any valid instruction-model program (loop, compare, if, return) generically. Level 4 block-built Linear Search should work through this shared engine, not bespoke wiring, and the single-block flow from F001 must keep working through the same code path with no new special case.

scope.scope_note: 2026-07-04: types.ts added to allowed_files (owner decision, see DECISIONS.md). True generalization threads a source-instruction reference through execution events, requiring an optional `source?: ProgramInstruction` field on ExecutionEvent. Backward-compatible.

evidence: 2026-07-04: npm test 38/38 pass (was 32; +6 M2 tests), build OK, lint clean, clean-state OK.

2026-07-04: Design - each execution frame now carries its source ProgramInstruction (optional field on ExecutionEvent, engine.ts threads it through). blockly.ts buildProgramCode() returns the Python plus a Map<instruction, lineNumber> keyed by object identity. getTeachingStep dispatches: single-block linearSearch keeps its fixed line mapping; block-built programs look up frame.event.source in the line map, so Level 4 and the single-block recipe share ONE engine with no duplicated per-line logic.

2026-07-04: getLearningSupport now recognizes the canonical block-built linear search shape (isSupportedBlockLinearSearch) and returns teaching/codeHighlight/explanation = supported for it; non-canonical Level 4 arrangements stay 'partial' with no fake highlight (unit tested both ways).

2026-07-04: Tests - blockly.test asserts the line map points at the right text for nested instructions; learningSupport.test runs the REAL engine on the canonical Level 4 program and asserts every sourced frame highlights exactly that instruction's line (scan->for, compare->compare line, if->if line, found->return i, missing->return -1), summary===event.message, and no supported step is ever left without a highlight. A test confirms the recipe and block builds return the same found index.

2026-07-04: Browser QA on Level 4 Teaching - stepping shows line 2 (for) on loop step, line 3 (compare) on compare, line 4 (if) with correct true/false explanation, line 5 (return i) on found, all synced with the active cell, pointer, trace, and explanation. 2026-07-04: Note - the F001 stale-switch guard means instructions is briefly [] on level change; a scripted rapid-click sequence can observe that transient empty program, but it settles correctly on any normal navigation (verified by clean reload -> Level 5 = 5 code lines, 14 frames). Not a product bug.

features.title: Problems mode: build blocks, Submit, grade against test cases
features.behavior: Add a Problems mode (alongside Puzzle/Sandbox) with one hand-authored problem ('Find the Target', linear search). The learner builds blocks and hits Submit; the program is graded against multiple test cases (found/missing/empty/first/last/duplicate) and a results panel shows N/M passed with real per-case data for failures. Grading is a pure function that calls executeProgram per case - no engine, blockly, or teaching changes. See docs/STAGE_2_LEETCODE.md.

scope.scope_note: Stage 2 must be additive/reuse-only: import executeProgram, blocks, and the teaching layer; do not edit them. engine/blockly/learningSupport are forbidden to enforce this. If a real edit is needed, stop and record why in DECISIONS.md before expanding scope.
